style: Say firmly but kindly, like a ship captain giving clear directions
lines: Our club's film keeps jumping. Tap Play, then step through it with the arrows.
Turn on Jump Finder. It lights up whatever changed since the last frame.
Find a frame where too much lit up, and tap Something jumped here.
Look at the Jump Finder. What lit up?
Step to the frame before, then back. Look at what changed before tagging again.
Only a small figure move changed here. Step to a different frame and look again.
Clean! Now go make your own. Tap Go to the studio.
Pick a story first. Four beats, start to end.
Set up your studio. Your choices show up later in the Jump Finder.
Move Moss a tiny bit, then tap Snap. Then do it again.
Tap Check to see if anything jumped.
Camera, light, hands and figure moves pass. Tap Play to check how your props move.
Some frames jumped. Tap a mark to see why.
Choose a title board and music, then tap Premiere to screen your film.
Lights down. Here we go.
Shoot some frames in Studio first, then come back to Premiere.
Move the selected figure between the two ghost images. Tap Keep in-between when both moves are small.
That still leaves a big jump. Move the figure between the two ghosts, then tap Keep in-between.
Tape the tripod's feet down, and don't lean on the table.
Close the blinds and use one lamp, so clouds can't change your light.
Use the remote, or take your hands back and wait one and a half seconds before you snap.
Move a little at a time. If the figure doesn't overlap its onion skin at all, the move is too big.
Everything moved, even the table. That's the camera.
The brightness changed across the whole picture, without moving.
That shape at the edge is a hand left in the shot.
A figure crossed a big gap between two pictures.
The strip holds forty-eight frames. Check your film, or reshoot a frame.
Your film is ready. Change a choice or tap Premiere to screen it again.
Drag the prop on the set, or use arrows on its button. Move it a little between snaps, just like the figures.
The frame is removed. Pose from the previous picture, then tap Snap to replace it.
Tap Shoot and capture at least two frames. Then tap Check to compare them.
Nothing jumped, but nothing moved yet. Tap Shoot, move a figure a little, then tap Snap.
Move Wren a tiny bit, then tap Snap. Then do it again.
